msg: CALIBRATION, and the one bound in this workspace that fixes a model parameter the datasheet does not state. A PLAIN unity-gain OPA2333 follower into CL = 1 nF must reproduce the roughly mid-30 % small-signal overshoot of SBOS351D Figure 15 (a GRAPH READ - the datasheet tabulates no capacitive-load number and its own table just says 'See Typical Characteristics'). Measured 32.0 %, which is what fixes ro = 1.0 kohm. If this bound moves, every conclusion about the output stage - including the P4 decision to remove R6 - moves with it. It must not be deleted.
CALIBRATION. Figure 15 shows overshoot staying around 0-5 % out to 100-200 pF. Measured 0.0 % at CL = 100 pF.

CALIBRATION of the BRACKET. With ro = 2 kohm - TI's literal open-loop output impedance, stated only at f = 350 kHz - the same unity buffer overshoots 45.5 %, MORE than Figure 15. That is how the 2 kohm bracket is known to be pessimistic rather than merely different, and it bounds ro from above.

DESIGN TARGET. THE SHIPPING OUTPUT STAGE: U2B at G2 = 3.49 with NO isolation resistor, driving the full 1 nF REQUIREMENTS Q8 allows, calibrated ro. Measured 6.60 %, about 63 degrees of phase margin; 12 % is about 55 degrees. THIS is the measurement that removed R6 - the Figure 15 curve that motivated the part is a UNITY-GAIN measurement (os_ub2 = 32 % under identical conditions), and U2B's noise gain of 3.49 moves the loop crossover from 350 kHz to 100 kHz.

DESIGN TARGET, shipping stage on the pessimistic ro = 2 kohm bracket: 17.94 %, about 50 degrees of phase margin. 25 % is about 41 degrees - still unconditionally stable, which is where the acceptance line is drawn. The board is stable into the specified cable on EITHER end of the ro bracket with no isolation resistor.
DESIGN TARGET. Control: no cable, no overshoot. Measured 0.0 %.
Same control on the pessimistic bracket. Measured 0.0 %.

EVIDENCE, kept from the R6 comparison: the 100 R fitted at P3 gave 6.28 % against 6.60 % with none - 0.3 points. An out-of-loop series R has authority only in proportion to riso/ro, so against an ro of 1-2 kohm a 100 R does essentially nothing. That, plus the unity-gain premise being wrong, is the whole case for the removal.
EVIDENCE: riso = 1 kohm - comparable to ro at last - halves the overshoot to 3.19 %. This is what a working isolation resistor would have looked like, and what the board decided it does not need.
EVIDENCE GUARD, not a board bound: overshoot at riso = 0 minus riso = 1 k on the calibrated ro, measured +3.41 points. Guards the sign of the ungated comparison sweep.
Same evidence guard, pessimistic bracket: +9.36 points.
